subject: Finsight renewal: capacity recommendation, ROI recap & next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finsight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Finsight renewal: capacity recommendation, ROI recap & next steps

Hi Aisha,

Following up on our usage review for the FinSight account — thanks again for sharing the Q1 job-level logs. I pulled together a short recap of token spend trends, tail-latency events, and an ROI model for a stepped commit that we think maps to your growth curve. Key highlights: 

- Monthly token consumption (Mar–May): 1.2M -> 1.8M -> 2.7M tokens. Peak batch jobs accounted for ~35% of the delta.
- Overages in April triggered a 17% higher bill vs committed units; projected to recur without commit adjustment.
- Observed 95th latency spikes during large inference batches (attached latency traces).

Recommendation (high level): a 12-month stair-step commit: 2M tokens/month for Q3, 3M/month for Q4–Q1, with optional burst capacity for peak ETL windows. That commit reduces unit cost by ~28% vs current on-demand and cushions you against overage spikes.

I attached the Q1 usage report and a pricing model workbook that shows the net savings and a simple ROI (payback in ~2.6 months on current run-rate if usage continues).

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the numbers and align on procurement timing? If procurement prefers, we can issue a term amendment + DocuSign link once you're ready.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Finsight_Q1_usage_report.pdf, commit_pricing_model.xlsx

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finsight renewal: capacity recommendation, ROI recap & next steps

On 2027-05-22 Aisha Khan wrote:
> Thanks Logan — this is helpful. Quick clarifying items before we loop in procurement:
> 1) Can you confirm how overage credits would be applied during Q3 if we start the stair-step mid-quarter?
> 2) We noticed latency spikes impacting our nightly batch scoring jobs; can you include a short performance mitigation plan (e.g., burst capacity vs different batching config) with cost delta?

Hi Aisha — good questions. Short answers up front: 

1) Overage/proration: if the stair-step starts mid-quarter we prorate committed units for that partial period; any overages for that partial month would be treated as standard overage rates but we can offer a one-time courtesy credit equal to the delta between prorated commit and your last-month overage (we often do this for customers who migrate to a commitment mid-cycle). I'll note that as a term in the amendment draft we prepare for procurement.

2) Performance mitigation: two paths we recommend depending on operational preference:
  - Short-term (no infra change): enable temporary burst capacity for scheduled nightly windows (1–3 hours). Estimated incremental cost: ~$1,250/week for the windows you described; reduces 95th latencies to baseline.
  - Mid-term (recommended): switch those batch pipelines to dedicated GPU pool during ETL windows (Redwood Dedicated). That eliminates noisy-neighbor effects and stabilizes p95, with an incremental monthly delta but a lower per-token unit cost for heavy batch usage.

I've attached a small sensitivity sheet (commit_pricing_model.xlsx) that shows total cost under three scenarios: current on-demand, 12-mo stair-step + burst windows, and Dedicated-pool hybrid. The ROI column shows net savings vs baseline after credits and commit discounts.

If Wednesday 5/24 11am PT works, I'll invite Ben and Marissa to join to handle procurement and AM questions.

Regards,
Logan

Attachments: commit_pricing_model.xlsx, latency_traces-20270430.zip
